head.h1: Beach Catering in Dubai — Menus, Prices and What's Included

opening_paragraph: myCHEF beach catering in Dubai is a private chef, live grill and full table service on the sand, from AED 700 per person. Everything is brought straight to you. A vetted team fires up the BBQ, plates fresh food where your guests are sitting, and packs everything away afterwards — so your feet stay in the water and nobody spends the day carrying cool-boxes. Tell us your date and guest count, and you will have an itemised proposal, usually within one business day.

replace_in_block.new_heading: What is on a beach catering menu in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: A beach menu in Dubai is built around fresh, refreshing food that suits heat and sand — think grilled seafood, marinated meats, bright salads and fruit over heavy, saucy dishes. Our BBQ catering heart delivers prawns, lobster, sea bass, lamb chops, chicken skewers and juicy burgers straight off the flame, alongside mezze, grain salads, dips and warm flatbreads. For lighter grazing we build seafood towers, ceviche, chilled watermelon and sorbet; for beach food catering with kids in the group we add sliders, corn and easy grills the whole family knows. Menus are fully customisable and can be halal, vegetarian, vegan or allergen-aware on request. Whether you want a laid-back spread or a more luxury beach catering menu with premium seafood and a live oyster station, the chef designs it around your guests, the time of day and how long you plan to stay on the sand.

add_block.new_heading: What does beach catering in Dubai include?
new_paragraphs: Beach catering in Dubai includes everything needed to serve a proper meal on the sand: a chef, the food, the equipment and the cleanup. A typical booking covers menu design around your guests and the setting, a vetted private beach chef, live BBQ and grill stations, chilled drinks service, plus service staff for larger groups. Because there is rarely a kitchen nearby, the team arrives fully self-contained — portable grills, chafing units, prep stations, shade for the food, serviceware and waste removal are all part of the beach catering services we bring. Everything is chosen to hold up in sun, sand and sea breeze, so hot food stays hot and cold food stays safe. When the last plate is cleared, we strike the setup and leave the sand exactly as we found it — no trace, no rubbish, no cleanup left to you.

add_block.new_heading: Beach catering for weddings, corporate events and parties
new_paragraphs: Yes — beach catering works for weddings, corporate beach days and private parties alike, and the format flexes to each. For a beach wedding we run plated courses or elegant grazing stations with a dedicated chef and waiters; for corporate beach catering and team days we lean toward relaxed BBQ buffets and live stations that keep a crowd fed without stiff formality. Beach party catering — birthdays, sundowners, bachelor and bachelorette gatherings — sits somewhere in between: generous sharing platters, a grill running all afternoon and a menu built for barefoot eating. Whatever the occasion, beach catering for events is scaled to your headcount, from an intimate dozen to a couple of hundred guests. If your celebration moves between water and shore, pair it with pool party catering or a picnic setup so the whole day flows as one.

add_block.new_heading: The beach BBQ menu in full, course by course
new_paragraphs: What follows is a working beach grill menu in the order your guests eat it, not a sample. MyCHEF designs the menu and matches the chefs; the chefs and the licensed kitchens they work in cook the food. A typical booking draws five or six cold dishes, three or four hot starters, four or five grills, a seafood plate, the vegetarian course, two sides, breads and three desserts. Tell your planner how long you are staying on the sand and those counts move.
Cold mezze and salads, down before the coals are ready
Hummus, moutabal, baba ghanouj, muhammara, labneh with garlic.
Tabbouleh, fattoush, rocca with onion and tomato, rocca with feta cheese.
Vine leaves (warak enab), shanklish with thyme, hindbeh, mixed olives with pickled cucumber.
Quinoa tabouleh, freekeh salad, kale and quinoa, beetroot salad, three bean salad.
Greek salad, caprese, green apple coleslaw, potato salad, a fresh vegetable platter.
Mezze opens almost every Dubai grill for a practical reason: it holds its texture in the heat and can sit out while the fire settles.
Hot starters and pastries, while the grill comes up to heat
Fried kebbe, cheese sambousek, meat sambousek, spinach fatayer, cheese rolls.
Falafel, potato with coriander, makanek, sujouk, chicken wings.
Hummus fatteh, eggplant fatteh, kofta balls with pomegranate, mousakhan rolls.
Mini lahem beajine, and arayes kafta: flatbread packed with spiced minced meat and pressed straight onto the grill.
The mashawi grill, Arabic charcoal
Shish tawouk, lamb kabab, kabab khoush khash, kabab orfali, chicken kafta.
Lamb chops, lamb meat cubes, lamb loin, lahem meshwi, whole boneless chicken.
Mixed grill and full mixed grill, arayes, masbaha with pine nuts, grilled tomato and onion.
Makanek and sujouk carried over from the hot starters, finished over the coals.

The kebab names are not decoration. Khoush khash carries chilli through the mince, orfali is the pepper-heavy version, and kafta is a different grind again, so a menu listing three of them gives your guests three genuinely different plates, not one kebab described three ways.
Desi grill, seekh and tikka
Chicken seekh kebab, beef seekh kebab, chapli kebab, mutton ribs.
Tikka boti, malai boti, chicken tikka, fish tikka.
Paneer tikka and tandoori vegetables, fired in a tandoor.
Chicken karahi and mutton biryani alongside, for guests who want a curry with their grill.
Subcontinental hosts tend to brief by ratio, not by dish, two vegetarian mains to three non-vegetarian being the usual shape, and a menu is costed that way if you ask for it.
Continental cuts and steakhouse grills
Ribeye, picanha, Argentinian ribeye, Angus short rib, wagyu skirt steak, wagyu beef cheeks.
Tomahawk with rosemary and thyme gremolata, truffle butter, roast baby potatoes and vegetables.
Black Onyx tomahawk, carved at the table for a group to share.
Spiced chicken legs, honey glazed chicken wings, beef chorizo, schubling and cheese knacker sausage.
Brisket sliders on soft potato buns with truffle aioli, caramelised onions, pickles and parmesan, plus plain beef and chicken sliders for younger guests.
Grilled seafood, the course that belongs on a beach
Grilled jumbo shrimp, tiger prawn skewers, salmon skewers, mixed seafood skewers.
Grilled hammour fillet, BBQ hammour, herb marinated fish, salmon fillet, smoked ocean trout.
Fried calamari, octopus provencal, lobster tail tacos, whole lobster.
Fish sayadieh or seafood paella, when you want one wide pan the whole table digs into.
Vegetarian and vegan grill, a full course and not a footnote
Grilled halloumi, paneer tikka, marinated mushrooms, grilled peppers.
Vegetable skewers, zucchini and eggplant, asparagus and artichoke, shiitake mushroom, negima spring onion.
BBQ corn on the cob, grilled vegetables, sauteed vegetables, falafel, vegetarian burgers.
Smokehouse, low and slow
Prime brisket, salt and pepper brisket, smoked wagyu brisket, wagyu smoked beef ribs.
Pastrami, pulled lamb, lamb leg, smoked whole chicken, duck, beef chorizo.
Sides of mandi rice, coleslaw, potato salad, three bean salad and potato buns.
Pork does not appear anywhere on this menu. Pulled lamb, beef ribs and beef chorizo do that job instead, and the food is halal as standard.
Robata skewers, the charcoal theatre course
Chicken yakatori, teba chicken wing, tsukune chicken balls, tsukune shrimp.
Scallop, shrimp, salmon, short rib, beef yakatori, wagyu skirt steak.
Enoki with short rib, asparagus with short rib, beef with asparagus.
Shiitake mushroom, negima spring onion, zucchini and eggplant, tomato with white asparagus.
Robata is counted in pieces per guest, not by weight, so the quantity landing on the table is a number you agree in advance instead of a surprise.
A centrepiece worth photographing
Whole roasted lamb carved at a station, oriental, biryani or friki style.
Half lamb, lamb leg, roasted baby leg of lamb, mutton ra'an.
Lamb ouzi and mansaf kharouf, set on spiced rice.
Whole turkey with oriental rice, or slow-roasted beef ribeye carved to order.

A whole lamb feeds roughly thirty guests and gives an evening its photograph. On a beach it also solves a practical problem, because one carving station serves a crowd faster than skewers coming off a grill one round at a time.
Rice, hot sides and breads
White basmati, biryani rice, arabic rice, chicken or lamb kabseh, chicken freekeh, moghrabieh with meat and chicken.
Roasted potatoes, country potato, battat fries, cajun sweet potato fries, herbed couscous.
Fasolia bil zeit, bamieh bil zeit, collard greens with green beans, grilled tomato and onion.
Fresh arabic bread and kaak, manakeesh with zaatar, cheese or meat from a saj station, and naan from the tandoor.
Sauces and relishes, named individually
Garlic toum, chimichurri, gremolata, mustard, creamy BBQ.
House-made tomato relish, beetroot relish, yoghurt with cucumber and mint.
Peach habanero BBQ sauce, marmalade smoked tonkatsu BBQ sauce, maple syrup chilli pineapple vanilla relish.
Dessert
Cheese kunafa, halawet el jibben, othmalieh with cheese or kashta, znood el sit.
Umm ali, mafroukeh, maamoul bil ashta, mixed baklawa, katayef kashta.
Mohalabieh, halawet el riz, creme caramel, cheesecake, tiramisu, macarons.
Sliced fruit platter and fresh fruit salad, which is what most guests reach for after an afternoon in the sun.
The same dishes, served six different ways

The menu above does not change with the format, only the way it reaches your guests. A live grill station puts a grillmaster on the sand cooking to order. A buffet brings the same food hot into chafing dishes. Plated service suits a smaller dinner where every course is timed. Drop-off arrives in portioned boxes with no staff at all. A grazing table lays the spread out flat for a garden or a beach club terrace. A reception format shrinks the grill to finger food: mini shish tawouk, mini kafta, mini grilled meat and mini shawarma. Alongside the grill you can run a shawarma station, a saj bread station, a falafel station, a tandoor, a rotisserie or a carving station, each with a chef working in front of your guests. At a permitted event on beach land all six run; on an open public beach the carving and rotisserie stations run and the fired ones stay in the licensed kitchen, which is the difference the next section is about.
Dietary variants, stated plainly

Halal is standard here, which in Dubai is table stakes, not a selling point. Vegetarian dishes have their own course above instead of being buried in a footnote, and the vegan choices sit inside it: falafel, vegetable skewers, tandoori vegetables, grilled corn, sauteed vegetables, grilled peppers. Gluten-free is where this whole category is weak. Most Dubai grill menus accommodate it without itemising which dishes qualify, so ask, and your planner will confirm dish by dish with the kitchen preparing your food rather than hand you a blanket assurance. Nut, dairy and shellfish allergies work the same way, in writing, before the date. Documentation for the kitchen handling your booking is provided on request.
Fire on a Dubai beach, and which of the four situations yours is

"Beach" is four different rulebooks in Dubai, and the live-fire answer changes with each one. On an open public beach — Kite Beach, the open JBR stretch, Umm Suqeim — lighting a fire outside a designated zone is a Dubai Municipality offence carrying a Dh500 fine, so nothing fired runs there and the menu is built on live carvery, the raw bar and an electric plancha line, none of which need a flame. In a Dubai Municipality beach park, charcoal is permitted at the fixed BBQ stations and only there, not on a cook line carried in and set up on the grass. At a permitted private event on beach land the full repertoire is available — charcoal, tandoor, robata, smoker, saj and shawarma spit — with every fired station laid out as an open-air island clear of the marquee fabric and the gas permit applied for alongside the event permit rather than after the menu is signed. At a private beach club the fire code is already satisfied by the venue's own approved line, and the only gate left is the operator's sign-off. MyCHEF establishes which of the four your beach is before quoting, and the menu is designed against that answer instead of around it.

Where a setup does not travel, the replacement is named rather than the dish dropped. Tandoor breads and tikka are fired in the licensed kitchen and finished hot at the counter, so naan still arrives blistered. The robata card — binchotan skewers, tare glazes, the whole list — runs on an electric yakitori griddle with the same counter and the same to-order rhythm; only the charcoal aroma changes. Smokehouse cuts are smoked off site the day before, held hot and carved live on the sand, which is the part guests actually stand and watch. The saj switches to an electric dome that needs no gas permit and rolls the same manakeesh in front of you. The raw bar and the carving station need no heat source at any beach in Dubai, which is exactly why they anchor an open-public-beach menu rather than fill it out.
A beach restaurant table, or the grill on your own stretch of sand?

Plenty of people weighing up this page are also looking at a beach restaurant or a beach club table, whether that is Palm Jumeirah, Dubai Marina, JBR, Jumeirah or a quieter beach side spot further down the coast. The trade is control. A restaurant fixes the menu, the sitting time and the number of covers, and you fit your group around it. Catering on the sand runs the other way: your guests keep the stretch of beach they are already on, the menu is picked dish by dish from the courses above, timings follow your sunset rather than a second seating, and the clear-down belongs to somebody else. For a group of eight a restaurant usually wins on convenience. From about twenty guests upward, once a restaurant starts quoting minimum spends and set menus, the grill coming to you is the one that bends to your day.

add_block.new_heading: How does setup, permits and cleanup work on Dubai's beaches?
new_paragraphs: The practical side is handled for you: setup, safe cooking and full cleanup are built into every beach catering booking. For private villa beaches, hotel beaches and residence access, we coordinate arrival, parking and load-in directly with the venue. For public beaches such as Kite Beach or the open stretches of Jumeirah, we advise on the permissions and any permits required, and the chefs and partner kitchens we work with operate to Dubai Municipality food-safety requirements for outdoor cooking and cold-chain handling. Timing matters on the sand — we schedule around tides, sunset and the cooler parts of the day, and bring shade, food covers and proper temperature control so nothing spoils. Power, water, waste and equipment come with the team, so you are not sourcing generators or hunting for a tap. After service everything is broken down, bagged and removed, leaving the beach clean.

add_block.new_heading: Why book beach catering with myCHEF?
new_paragraphs: MyCHEF was founded by a chef trained in some of Europe's most demanding kitchens, on one idea: you own the day, we carry the work. No chef is offered for beach catering before clearing identity checks, a practical cooking assessment, reference verification and ongoing performance reviews — a continuous standard, not a one-time tick. We are honest about it, too: no system removes every risk, so we match each event to the best available chef for it.

For a beach BBQ or seafood spread, that is often Ahmed Al-Rashid — 18+ years across Dubai, London and Paris in classical French technique — who designs each menu as a collaboration with the host, every course timed, seasoned and served to exacting standards. We have run beach catering alongside villa weddings, yacht celebrations and corporate galas across Dubai. Comparing formats first? Read private chef vs catering .

add_block.new_heading: Common questions about beach catering in Dubai
new_paragraphs: How much does beach catering cost in Dubai?
It's from AED 700 per person, quoted by guest count, menu and service level. A relaxed grill buffet costs less than a plated seafood dinner with full staff. Send your details for an itemised quote.
What is included in beach catering?
Included is menu design, a vetted chef, service staff where needed, all equipment, setup and full cleanup — the team arrives self-contained and leaves the sand as they found it.
Do you provide beach catering for weddings and corporate events?
Yes — we cater beach weddings, corporate beach days, birthdays and private parties, scaling the chef and service team to your guest count and the formality you want.
Can you cook fresh on the beach?
Yes — the chefs we work with run live BBQ and grill stations on the sand, cooking to order instead of delivering pre-made trays, so food is served hot and fresh.
Do you handle beach permits and food safety?
For private and hotel beaches we coordinate access with the venue; for public beaches we advise on the permissions needed and work within Dubai Municipality food-safety rules.
Which Dubai beaches do you cover?
All of Dubai — including JBR, Palm Jumeirah, Kite Beach, Jumeirah and private villa and hotel beaches. Tell us your spot and we will confirm access and logistics.
How do I hire beach catering in Dubai?
Share your date, guest count and beach; we send an itemised proposal, usually within one business day, then confirm your chef and team.

Confirm your beach catering menu about 7 days out, when the guest list is firm.
